records.name: Philadelphia Lawyers for Social Equity
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives free legal help to low-income Philadelphians clear old criminal records so they can get jobs and housing. It also trains volunteers and works with community partners on pardon help.
records.what_you_do: Attend a short volunteer training (the site says about 45 minutes), get help with an expungement or pardon if you qualify, or invite the group to speak to your organization.

schedule.text: No weekly hours are published. Intake clinics and volunteer trainings are announced on the Events page.

first_step.how: Email info@plsephilly.org to book help or ask about the next intake clinic, since the office does not take walk-ins.
first_step.basis: Help is free for people who qualify and volunteer trainings are open to the public, but you must book ahead, and the phone line is down during the office move.
first_step.what_to_expect: You contact the office before you come, since walk-ins are not taken. Intake happens at clinics announced on the Events page, and the clinic schedule and sign-up sit in an outside portal the page links to. The site says a volunteer training takes about 45 minutes.
first_visit_tips: Email first, because the phones are out of service during the office move.
Check the Events page for the next intake clinic and follow its registration link.
Confirm the new office address before you go, since the group is moving.

records.notes: Phone number left out: the site says phones are temporarily out of service during the move. The site also lists a second email at a different organization's domain, which was not added. No clinic hours or fees are published. The site's dated items are COVID-era notices and a footer copyright, so the 2026-10 date is carried from tier 1 and no newer dated item was found this pass. Clinic registration sits in an outside portal, which was not opened.

records.name: Philadelphia Medical Reserve Corps
records.summary: A city volunteer unit that helps during public health emergencies, disasters, and big public events such as the marathon. You do not need a medical background to join.
records.what_you_do: Register online with the state, pass a background check, and attend an orientation, which is strongly encouraged before any deployment. Then take trainings and get called for deployments when needed. Medical volunteers give screenings, medicines, or vaccines; others answer phones, do data entry, or interpret.

schedule.text: Deployments are called as needed. The city encourages volunteers to join at least one training, exercise, or deployment each year.

first_step.how: Register on the state volunteer site (serv.pa.gov), choose Philadelphia MRC, and pass the background check before you attend orientation.
first_step.basis: Open to adults 18 and up, but you apply, pass a background check, and get accepted before orientation, so you see the work only after approval.
first_step.what_to_expect: Acceptance can take a few days or weeks after you apply, since the background check runs first. Orientation is held one or two times a year, in person or online, and it is strongly encouraged before any deployment. After that you are invited to trainings, exercises, and real deployments as they come up, so the work varies.
first_visit_tips: Use your legal first and last name exactly as on your birth certificate or photo ID, because the check matches it.
Have your date of birth and your occupation ready for the online form.
Watch your email, since acceptance and training notices come that way.

records.notes: Newcomer rating moved from 3 to 2 because applicants must be accepted and background-checked before the orientation where the work is explained. The city page does not say who pays for the background check, how long orientation runs, or how often volunteers are called. The page has no dated items, so status stays probably_active. Email address and phone are as published on the city page.

records.name: Philadelphia Metro Wildlife Center
records.summary: A licensed wildlife rehabilitation center that takes in injured and orphaned wild animals from Philadelphia and nearby counties. Its volunteers do much of the daily feeding and cleaning.
records.what_you_do: Prepare food, feed the animals, clean cages, and wash dishes and laundry on a regular weekly shift. Some volunteers help clinic staff with animal care.

schedule.text: Volunteers take one four-hour shift a week in a fixed time slot, all year round. The center is open daily from 9 am to 5 pm.

cost.text: Volunteering is unpaid, and there is no fee to bring in an animal

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer interest form on the center's Volunteer page, or call (267) 416-9453 to ask about volunteering and the wait-list.
first_step.basis: Volunteers apply through an interest form and go on a wait-list because the center is at capacity, and the page gives no timeline.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers are adults, 18 and older, who take a regular four-hour shift each week all year. The work is mostly care: preparing food, feeding, cleaning cages, dishes, and laundry, with some help for clinic staff. Visits are by appointment only, so call before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call (267) 416-9453 or email info@phillywildlife.org before you visit, since admission is by appointment.
Ask about the wait-list and shift times when you call, because the site does not give either.
Call staff before you bring in any injured or orphaned animal, since the center asks for a call first.

records.notes: The center is in Norristown (Montgomery County), outside the city. Its site says it serves Philadelphia, Montgomery, Chester and Delaware counties, so it stays in. Tier 1 described an education and wildlife ambassador program; no page read this pass describes one, so that claim was removed from what_you_do. Orientation, training, parking, transit and accessibility are not described on the site. The 2020 and 2023 patient counts were not used as current. A 2026 newsletter is linked from the homepage but was not opened, so last_sign_of_life carries the tier 1 date.

records.name: Philadelphia More Beautiful Committee Clean Block Program
records.summary: Block captains and the city's More Beautiful Committee organize Saturday cleanups by police district each spring and summer, working with the Department of Sanitation. A yearly Clean Block Contest judges a set of registered blocks, and every contest block receives cash.
records.what_you_do: Join your block's Saturday cleanup and bag the litter for pickup, or ask PMBC for a block captain petition, which needs signatures from 51% of the residents on your block, one adult per household.

schedule.text: Saturday cleanups by police district, held each year between March and August. Your block captain sets the date with the clean block officer for your police district.

first_step.how: Call PMBC at (215) 685-3971 to find out whether your block has a captain and when your police district's Saturday is.
first_step.basis: Residents join through their block captain, and PMBC publishes a phone line to find one, so the way in is clear but needs a call first.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup is a Saturday on your block, run by your block captain with the clean block officer for your police district. PMBC can provide tools, supplies, and street cleaning help, and residents pick up litter and bag it for pickup. The site does not give a start time or how long the cleanup takes.
first_visit_tips: Bag the litter and set the bags at either end of the block for pickup.
Do not sweep trash or dirt into storm drains, and keep cars off the street while you work.
Bulk or household trash is not collected on cleanup Saturdays, so keep it out of the bags.

records.notes: Audience changed from public to residents: cleanups and the block captain role are for residents of registered blocks. Phone (215) 685-3971 appears on the program and block captain pages; the 2026 contest page lists (215) 685-3981, so confirm the number before wider use. The 2026 schedule lists cleanup Saturdays from March 7 to August 15 by police district; those dates are not in schedule.text. The 2026 contest prizes are $1,000 for first, $700 second, $500 third, $300 fourth, and $150 for each other contest block, with judging on Saturdays October 3, 10, 17 and 24, 2026 and a banquet on November 20 (year not printed, presumed 2026). Start time and cost are not stated, so cost is left out.

records.name: The Philadelphia Project
records.summary: A faith-based nonprofit that runs free home repairs for homeowners in several Northwest Philadelphia ZIP codes, including Germantown and Mt. Airy. Volunteers join short service trips, and volunteer teams do most of the repair work.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a service trip such as a day of service, a blitz weekend, or a summer of service, or apply for a repair through the Home Repair page if you own and live in an eligible home.

schedule.text: Service trips run through the year, including a summer of service, blitz weekends, spring break, and days of service. Most home construction happens in summer.

locations.label: Home repair area (Northwest Philadelphia ZIP codes)

cost.text: Homeowner repairs are free. The site does not say what volunteer trips cost.

first_step.how: Use the 'Tell Me More' inquiry form on the service trips page to ask about a day of service or a summer trip that fits your group.
first_step.basis: Trips are listed publicly and open to groups of many kinds, and the inquiry form is the way in, but the page does not say what skills are needed or what happens after the inquiry.
first_step.what_to_expect: A trip lasts from one day to a full week, and groups can be small, corporate, family, or intergenerational. Volunteers work on home repairs, church projects, children's programs, or service at food banks and shelters, and each trip includes an evening worship session. The site does not say what trips cost or where groups stay.
first_visit_tips: Pick a trip that fits your age: a day of service is open to all ages, summer trips and blitz weekends are mostly for grades 6 to 12, and spring break is for college students.
Ask the office what a trip costs and where people sleep, since the site does not say.
For a home repair, check the eligibility list on the Home Repair page before you apply.

records.notes: Office address 8230 Ridge Ave comes from the contact page; no phone or email is published on the pages read. Home repair eligibility on the Home Repair page: owner-occupied homes in listed ZIP codes, property taxes current, and household income under the HUD very low income limits (the page lists 2024 figures). Renters are not mentioned. Tier 1 named only Germantown and Mt. Airy, and the ZIP list is wider. Trip costs, lodging, and homes repaired per year are not stated. A 2022 meal sign-up link on the volunteer page was not used. Partner churches and the construction partner are not named, so there are no leads.

records.name: Philadelphia Scenic Works
records.summary: A nonprofit scene shop that builds sets and scenery for arts groups and trains people who want backstage careers. It runs a free High School Tech Theatre Club and free one-day skills workshops for the public.
records.what_you_do: Join the free High School Tech Theatre Club on Wednesdays, take a free one-day skills workshop, or join the mailing list to hear about apprenticeships and openings.

schedule.text: The High School Tech Theatre Club meets on Wednesdays from 4:30 to 5:45 pm during each school term. Skills workshops and apprenticeships come up on their own schedule.

locations.label: High School Tech Theatre Club (InterAct Theatre at The Drake)

cost.text: The High School Tech Theatre Club and the public skills workshops are free.

first_step.how: Fill out the High School Tech Theatre Club sign-up form linked from the top of the group's website.
first_step.basis: The club page says no experience is required and gives a sign-up form, and the club is free.
first_step.what_to_expect: The club meets on Wednesdays for about an hour and a quarter during each school term, at InterAct Theatre at The Drake. You learn tech theatre skills such as scenery, props, stage management, lighting, sound, and costumes. The club is free, and the page says no experience is needed.
first_visit_tips: Sign up through the form before the term starts, since the page does not list session dates.
The club meets at 302 S. Hicks Street, not at the Yeadon shop.
Send questions to the general email address on the contact page.

records.notes: The shop address is in Yeadon (Delaware County), outside the city, but the club and the workshops are in Philadelphia, so the group stays in. The club time is marked with an asterisk the site does not explain. The site says sessions run each school term without listing dates. The apprenticeship was closed to applications when checked. The 2026 Flower Show mention and the undated '01/18' post are not dated evidence, so last_sign_of_life carries the tier 1 date. InterAct Theatre is named as the club venue but has no link on the page, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Philadelphia Red Hat User Group
records.summary: A local group for people who use Red Hat and open source tools. Members get together for talks and hands-on sessions, as part of Red Hat's user group program.
records.what_you_do: Attend the talks and sessions, meet other technical users, and learn how Red Hat tools are used in real work.

schedule.text: Meets as scheduled sessions, each announced on Red Hat's listing with its own registration link.

cost.text: Free to register, as shown on the Red Hat event listing

first_step.how: Register through the link on Red Hat's events listing for the next Philadelphia session, or check the group's Meetup page for how it runs.
first_step.basis: Red Hat says its user group gatherings are open to anyone regardless of skill level, and each session has a registration link, but the venue is not on the listing.
first_step.what_to_expect: The listed session runs from 3 to 6 pm, about three hours, with talks and hands-on sessions. You will meet people who use Red Hat and open source tools in their work. You register ahead of time, and the listing does not show where the session is held.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead through the link on Red Hat's listing, since each session asks for it.
Check the registration page for the venue, because the listing does not show one.
Bring your own questions about Red Hat or open source tools, since the sessions focus on how people use them.

records.notes: The tier 1 website URL (https://www.redhat.com/en/red-hat-user-group) returned 404 today, so the North America page is used instead. The Red Hat listing shows a 3 to 6 pm session on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, with no venue, host, or price. The free price is carried from tier 1 and was not shown on the listing read today, so confirm it on the registration page. The open-to-the-public rating rests on Red Hat's general statement about user group gatherings, not one specific to Philadelphia, so newcomer friendliness is 3. The Meetup page was not read because Meetup is a lead platform. The phrase 'in person' was dropped from the summary because the venue is not published.
